findings.claim: M32's drill-down replan adopts a plan without running M31's plan_gap lint, so a mid-run drill-down can add a second enumeration and the run reports success / verdict PASS with an unranked list of lists — the exact defect ADR-018 Decision 3 names, re-opened through the adoption point that same ADR names by hand as the one that must lint.
findings.evidence: src/browser/agent.py:1006 `steps = steps[:si] + new_steps` in the drill-down branch has no plan_gap call, while the family-2 branch at agent.py:1078 does. ADR-018:157-158: 'A future adoption point (M32's observe replan) has to lint too; that is the invariant, not the two call sites.' specs/001-browser-contract.md:222-224 and agent.py:1109-1111 both assert the lint runs at every adoption point; agent.py:1110-1111 additionally asserts 'More than one enumeration never reaches here for an aggregate task' — false on the merged tree. Task 'Which product on this page has the most customer reviews?' (matches is_aggregate), fixture shop.html, stub_plans [[{extract_all, role:link, rank:true}, {observe, role:list, name:Catalogue}], [{extract_all, role:listitem, rank:true}]]. First plan passes the lint; the observe triggers the drill-down replan; the replan is adopted unlinted; two enumerations execute. verifier.aggregate_needs_comparison (verifier.py:553-556) is satisfied because a ranked extract_all is in the graded trace, so the backstop does not fire, and the judge is never reached as a rejector because L1 passed. Observed: status success, replans 1, verdict PASS, answer [[4 names],[4 name+price strings]].
findings.repro: reviewer's probe scratchpad/hunt.py. Proof of missing coverage: adding the lint at that adoption point makes the probe end non-success AND leaves the committed suite at 146/146 = 1.000 — no existing case can see that adoption point at all.
findings.acceptance: plan_gap(task, steps[:si] + new_steps) runs at the drill-down adoption point; a new adversarial case with those stub plans is watched red first, then asserts a non-success terminal status plus trace_actions / replans pinning the refusal at replan time; agent.py:1109-1111 and specs/001-browser-contract.md:223 updated to say three adoption points, not two.

findings.claim: ADR-020 cites a RED live report as the evidence for a 'live suite 9/9 after this change' claim, and the citation was re-pointed onto that red report inside this review's surface.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-020-m32-observation-drill-down.md:243-244 reads '(live suite 9/9 after this change, evals/report/20260822-234757-live.json)'. That report is score 0.888... = 8/9 with live-ol-edition-title failing. The next sentence excuses a different run with a different failing case. git diff 5a88b9c HEAD shows the citation moved in this window: -20260822-185648-live.json / +20260822-234757-live.json. The report 185648 was renamed to, 20260822-192844-live.json, IS 9/9, as is 20260823-155452-live.json. Seven red live reports sit on this branch; the ADR describes one. report-citations-resolve cannot catch this — its own docstring says it checks the citation RESOLVES, not that the number attached is an honest measurement.
findings.repro: .venv/bin/python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('evals/report/20260822-234757-live.json'));print(d['score'],[r['id'] for r in d['results'] if not r['passed']])" -> 0.888... ['live-ol-edition-title']
findings.acceptance: The 9/9 claim cites a report whose score is 1.0, or the sentence states the real score of the report it names. Optionally extend report-citations-resolve so a citation attached to a green claim must resolve to a green report.

findings.severity_note: Raised from the reviewer's LOW by the orchestrator: the reviewer extrapolated a CI band, and CI then measured this tree at 88.39s against 90 — 1.8% margin against a runner spread the repo records as 6.8%. The prediction became a measurement, which makes it a published-honesty item rather than a speculation.
findings.claim: ADR-021 leaves CI's fast ceiling at 90 un-re-derived while the tree grew from the 116-case tree CI's 90 was measured on to 146 cases, putting CI at roughly the same margin the repo twice ruled a coin flip.
findings.evidence: ADR-021 states CI's EVAL_WALL_BUDGET_S_FAST stays 90 'because CI has produced no fast run on this tree' — accurate when written, and .github/workflows/eval.yml is byte-identical to origin/main. CI has since run: run 32627229208, fast 146/146 = 1.000 at 88.39s, invariant 54/54 at 16.79s / 20. fast-wall-clock-budget's provenance item (9) calls the previous CI number 'the next coin flip at 8% margin against a 6.8% runner spread'; 88.39 against 90 is 1.8%.
findings.acceptance: ADR-021 records the real CI measurement and its margin explicitly, so a red CI run on the next case added is a predicted event rather than a surprise. Raising CI's number is a separate human decision and is NOT in scope here.

findings.claim: ADR-019's republished bands each drop one recorded run and the invariant derivation sentence applies the +15% rule to the second-slowest run rather than the slowest it just published.
findings.evidence: ADR-019:88-90 publishes 'Slowest recorded invariant run at 54 cases: 13.85s' then says 'The same rule gives 13.56 x 1.15 = 15.6 -> 20' — 13.56 is the second-slowest. At HEAD the ledger holds 15 invariant runs at 54 cases (13.16 missing from the ADR list) and 13 fast runs at 146 cases (74.45 missing from the ADR's 12-run list). Both derived ceilings are unaffected (13.85 x 1.15 -> 20; 74.81 x 1.15 = 86.03 -> 90), and published-band-matches-the-ledger passes because eval_adapter.py:428-437 only compares the published maximum, never the run list.
findings.acceptance: The derivation sentence applies the rule to the slowest run it publishes, and each band lists every run the ledger holds at that case count, or says explicitly that it is a snapshot taken before the commit's own gate runs.
findings.route_note: LOW; neither half changes a derived or enforced ceiling. Same band-vs-ledger drift class as PR #29 R21.
